status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: watch virtual or a demonstration of pushing and pulling activities in physical activities,
demonstrate pushing and pulling activities,
practise pushing and pulling activities,
sing songs while pulling and pushing,
play games using pulling and pushing skills by observing safety.
key_inquiry_questions: How can pulling and pushing skills be applied at home?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital literacy: the learner manipulates digital devices to watch clips showing pushing and pulling activities.
Self-efficacy: the learner appreciates their ability to demonstrate and practise pushing and pulling successfully.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner cooperates with others as they perform pushing and pulling activities.
Respect: the learner portrays positive regard for self and others as they practise pushing and pulling activities.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: The learner individually observes safety while playing games involving pushing and pulling.
sub_strands.links: Mathematical activities: the learner counts while pulling and pushing.

outcomes.text: identify pushing and pulling in physical activities for space and body awareness
perform pulling and pushing activities for flexibility
enjoy pushing and pulling for strength and flexibility

learning_experiences: watch videos/pictures to recognise how to mix colour by spraying and blowing technique,
spray colours randomly using recyclable old brushes/improvised brushes and clean the hands after the activity,
mix the colour by blowing randomly using straws and a biro pen tube among others while observing safety,
draw and colour a simple composition using regular and irregular shapes,
paint a picture creatively for expression,
collaboratively, display their work for peer feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to clean the brush after painting?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: the learner watches videos with peers to recognises how to mix colours by using the spraying and blowing technique.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner explores colours mixing techniques in painting.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner respects others’ opinions while talking about their own and peers' pictures.
Social justice: the learner shares resources and responsibilities equitably while mixing coloured water paints.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion issues: the learner cleans the working area and washes hands after spraying paint.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: the learner takes care of hygiene by cleaning their hands after painting.

outcomes.text: identify colour mixing for familiarity
mix colours using spraying and blowing techniques
draw a picture using regular and irregular shapes
create a painting for self-expression
value drawing and painting for expression

content_topics: Short and long sounds (taa-aa-aa-aa taa-aa, taa and ta-te )
learning_experiences: sing simple familiar songs for familiarisation of short and long sounds used in creating their rhythmic patterns,
listen to or watch live or recorded performances of simple songs and clap their rhythmic patterns,
use short and long sounds to create simple rhythmic patterns using body percussion or a percussion instrument,
provide rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs using body percussion or a percussion instrument,
explore virtual sources to identify random and an all over patterns,
print a random pattern alternating colours to suggest rhythm, using
- a leaf
- block (banana stalk, maize cob, among others).
key_inquiry_questions: How can rhythms be created?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and imagination: the learner creates simple rhythmic patterns using short and long sounds.
Self-efficacy: the learner confidently plays rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of the digital devices as they record the rhythmic chant performances for future use.
Respect: the learner gives a chance to peers as they take turns to recite short and long sounds using French rhythm names.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: the learner portrays team spirit as they work with peers to create rhythms using short and long sounds on a percussion instrument or body percussion.
sub_strands.links: Mathematical Activities: the learner applies knowledge and skill of counting to maintain the beat as they accompany songs with rhythmic accompaniment.

outcomes.text: identify different sound durations in simple songs
create a simple rhythmic pattern using long and short sounds
improvise rhythmic accompaniment to simple songs using long and short sounds
make a random repeat pattern using found objects
appreciate creating rhythms and patterns

content_topics: Directions in Skipping (Forward, Backward, Right, Left
Pattern making (Straight line, curved, circular, zigzag).
learning_experiences: talk about skipping in different directions,
demonstrate skipping in different ways and directions,
practise skipping in different ways and directions with peers,
sing songs while skipping for enjoyment while making line patterns and shapes,
play games involving skipping activities with peers while observing safety,
share feedback about own and others performance in skipping.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are skipping activities interesting?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner pays attention to making patterns while skipping.
Self- efficacy: The learner individually skips confidently in different ways.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner cooperates with peers while skipping.
Peace: the learner avoids hurting others by observing safety while playing games involving skipping.
sub_strands.pcis: Gender issues in education: the learner shows respect for gender equality while playing games in skipping with peers.
sub_strands.links: Mathematical Activities: the learner learns concepts of shapes and patterns.

outcomes.text: identify different ways of skipping in different directions
skip in different directions for skill acquisition
make patterns while skipping in different ways
appreciate skipping in different directions for balance and strength

learning_experiences: observe images of simple collage from actual or virtual environment for motivation to make a collage,
collect varied recyclable materials for making collage,
sort out materials to make the collage,
outline a simple picture to guide the pasting of materials,
collaboratively, paste different materials on the outlined forms,
show and talk about own and others’ collage, work.
key_inquiry_questions: What materials can be used to make a collage?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: the learner works collaboratively to paste the different materials on the outlined forms,
Self-efficacy: the learner expresses themselves about their artwork during display sessions
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner uses recyclable materials from the environment responsibly.
Love: the learner shows and talk about their own and others’ collage, works.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: the learner develops self-awareness and self-esteem through display of their work and as they express their feelings, ideas and emotions.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: the learner uses locally available materials emphasising the concept of use of recycled/reusable materials.

outcomes.text: identify a collage for familiarity
prepare materials for making the collage
create a collage for self-expression
appreciate using collage as an art of self-expression

content_topics: Variation in rhythm, tempo (slow and fast), volume, (loud and soft), text, pitch,
learning_experiences: collaboratively listen to simple songs, noting variations in rhythm, volume, and speed in live or recorded performances and discuss them,
sing simple short songs and improvise variations in rhythm, tempo, volume, text and pitch,
use improvised pitched percussions such as bottles filled with water to different levels or two-tone wood blocks, to create melodic patterns,
collaboratively perform the created melodic patterns applying performance directions; slow/fast, soft/loud,
record the created melodies or play the melodies to peers for feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: How can a song be varied to make it more interesting?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner keenly listens to or watches live or recorded performances of simple songs and talks about the variations.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner creates melodic patterns from differently pitched objects.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: the learner provides feedback to peers’ performances using appropriate language.
Unity: the learner in groups researches from print and electronic media different simple ways of varying melodies.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety and Security: the learner observes their safety as they create melodic patterns from differently pitched objects.
Social Cohesion: the learner portrays team spirit as they find out from the electronic media different simple ways of varying melodies.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: the learner applies knowledge and skills gained in Environmental Activities to create melodic patterns from differently pitched objects.

outcomes.text: identify variations in a simple melodic pattern for aural skill development
create melodic patterns using improvised percussions
apply performance directions in performing simple songs
enjoy creating melodies using the variation technique

learning_experiences: observe actual or virtual samples of paper plain weaves of varied colours,
collect different coloured papers,
cut slits on a paper to make a paper loom,
cut paper strips of a different colour to the loom and dispose of waste responsibly,
interlace the strips by running over and under the slits on the paper frame to make paper mats in two colours,
experiment to make paper weaves with different colours,
showcase their plain weaves and ask their peers to comment.
key_inquiry_questions: Which other items can be woven?
Which other materials can be used for weaving?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner experiments to make paper weaves with different colours.
Learning to Learn: the learner acquires new skills in interlacing to make a woven item.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner disposes of paper cuttings after weaving.
Respect: the learner showcases their plain weaves and ask their peers to comment
sub_strands.pcis: Cultural Appreciation: the learner appreciates weaving as a traditional craft.
sub_strands.links: Environmental activities: the learner disposes of waste to maintain the environment.

outcomes.text: identify a plain paper weave for familiarity
create a plain paper weave to make
enjoy making paper mat using weaving

content_topics: Performance techniques; posture, accuracy of tune, clarity of words, entries and keeping to own part
learning_experiences: watch a variety of virtual or recorded clips on age-appropriate 2 and 3-part rounds and talk about what a round is,
talk about how to sing in a round focusing on; posture, accuracy of tune, clarity of words, entries and keeping to own part,
sing own part in a round on a specific theme for skill development,
sing rounds with peers applying appropriate performance techniques,
collaboratively, take turns to sing own part in a round as others give feedback,
talk about the message in a round sung.
key_inquiry_questions: How are rounds sung?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner talks about the round songs, and sings rounds with clear diction.
Self- efficacy: the learner sings own part in round songs on a specific theme for skill development.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner keeps to own part in a round performance.
Unity: the learner cooperates with others in groups while singing own part in round songs.
Respect: the learner portrays positive regard for self and others as they work in groups on rounds.
sub_strands.pcis:
Self-awareness and Self-esteem: the learner gains confidence as they sing round songs with appropriate performance techniques.
Social Cohesion: the learner works with peers while singing round songs in groups.
sub_strands.links:
English Language Activities: the learner applies the skill of communication acquired in English to clearly pronounce the words of the round.
Religious Activities: the learner applies values such as unity and love acquired in Religious Education during group work on rounds. 100 100

outcomes.text: aurally identify a round performance
sing own part in a round applying appropriate performance techniques
describe the message in a round
enjoy singing in a round

content_topics: Galloping movement Directions : forward, left and right.
Patterns: straight, curved, circular and zigzag.
learning_experiences: observe videos or demonstrations of galloping and talk about the body movement,
demonstrate galloping skills,
practise galloping in different directions,
practise galloping to make patterns,
play games while galloping in different directions,
give self and others feedback on their performance in galloping activities.
key_inquiry_questions: Which animals use galloping movement?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: the learner focusses on practising galloping skills by accepting feedback from peers.
Communication and collaboration: the learner interacts with peers while playing games that involve galloping.
sub_strands.values:
Love: the learner portrays respect in providing positive feedback to peers during practise of galloping activity.
Respect: the learner allows other chances while demonstrating galloping skills.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion: the learner embraces own and others performance during practise of galloping.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental activities: the learner learns about directions.
Religious activities: the learner learns positive values while providing feedback to peers. 102 102

outcomes.text: identify different directions of galloping for agility and coordination
perform galloping movement in different directions for skill acquisition
enjoy playing galloping games while moving in different directions

learning_experiences: observe actual or virtual samples of playing toys or dolls,
collaboratively, collect and sort different recyclable material for assemblage of toys or dolls,
safely, assemble the materials to get the structure of the doll or toy,
add details to enhance features of the toy or doll,
use the toys or dolls to play and sing with peers for enjoyment.
key_inquiry_questions: What local materials can be used to make a toy?
How can one join different materials to make a toy?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner use the toys or doll to play and sing with peers for enjoyment.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner assemble the materials to get the structure of the doll or toy.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: the learner gives positive feedback as they display items made.
Unity: the learner collaboratively, collect and sort different recyclable material for assemblage of toys or dolls.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety and security: the learner observes their safety by collecting and sorting different recyclable material assemblage of toys or dolls
Social Cohesion: the learner enjoys playing with peers using the toys or dolls created.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: the learner collect and sort different recyclable material for assemblage of toys or dolls. 104 104

outcomes.text: identify toys made by assemblage
make toys using assemblage
enjoy making and playing with the toys

learning_experiences: 1. How
watch video clips or a demonstration of a forward roll and V-balance,
perform a forward roll and talk about how the body moves,
perform V balance and talk about different parts of the body used,
identify, collect and share simple reusable materials within the environment to be used as markers as they observe safety precautions,
improvise the markers using the collected reusable materials and paint them,
mark the field using the improvised markers,
practise forward roll and V-balance
play games using forward roll and V-balance in sequence.
key_inquiry_questions: can forward roll and V balances be used to improve flexibility and balance?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner identifies simple reusable materials to use in improvised markers.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner talks about different ways the body moves when performing forward roll and V-balance.
sub_strands.values:
Love: the learner appreciates their ability in practising the forward roll and V-balance.
Social justice: the learner shares materials equitably with peers for making markers.
sub_strands.pcis:
Personal Hygiene: the learner cleans the working area and stores markers after the performance.
Environmental conservation: the learner collects reusable materials.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental Activities: the learner observes hygiene while collecting and sharing simple reusable materials.
Religious Activities: the learner applies values while working in groups.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: a line on this page ran across two columns and was cut by position.

outcomes.text: identify body parts used for performing forward roll and V-balance in gymnastics
make markers for use during forward roll and V-balance performance in gymnastics
perform forward roll for skill acquisition
perform V-balance for skill acquisition
enjoy performing forward roll and V-balance for flexibility and balance. 105 105

content_topics: Identifying Fiddles/ground bows/mouth bow (name. community and method of playing),
learning_experiences: watch live or recorded performances and aurally and orally identify string instruments from Kenyan communities,
responsibly use digital devices or pictures to identify the local names of Indigenous string instruments from Kenyan communities,
improvise a Kenyan stringed instrument- either a fiddle, ground or mouth bow observing safety and hygiene by washing hands and cleaning the working area,
explore methods of playing the improvised string instruments,
practise producing sound from a string instrument.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to learn about string instruments from different communities?
Which materials can be used to improvise a string instrument?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner visually and aurally identities and talks about the string instruments from the recordings and pictures.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner uses locally available materials to improvise a string instrument.
Digital Literacy: the learner responsibly searches for local names of string instruments- fiddles, ground and mouth bows.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of digital devices as they search for information on string musical instruments.
Unity: The learner cooperates with others as they work in pairs to identify and talk about the string instruments from the recordings and pictures.
sub_strands.pcis:
Environmental Conservation: the learner responsibly uses locally available materials to improvise string instruments
Self-awareness and Self-esteem: the learner plays the string instrument for enjoyment.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: the learner identifies string instruments from different Kenyan communities. 108 108

outcomes.text: identify Indigenous string musical instruments from Kenyan communities
improvise a string musical instrument using available materials
play an improvised string instrument for enjoyment
value Indigenous string instruments from Kenyan communities

learning_experiences: explore virtual and actual samples of beaded ornaments,
roll clay or papier mâché to make pellets for beading and clean hands,
pierce the pellets to make a hole through for stringing
dry the beads under shade,
decorate the beads by painting,
pass a string to make a single-stranded necklace,
display the ornament for peers’ feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: What other materials can be used to make beads?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: the learner works with peers to prepare clay or papier mâché for modelling items.
Creativity and imagination: the learner creates a single-stranded necklace and a matching bracelet.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: the learner gives positive feedback as they display items made.
Unity: the learner displays the ornament for peers’ feedback.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety and security: The learner observes their safety as they fire the clay beads in an improvised kiln.
Social Cohesion: The learner portrays team spirit as they explore the pinch and pellet technique to make simple forms in pairs.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: The learner roll clay or papier mâché to make pellets for beading and clean hands. 110 110

outcomes.text: identify modelled beads for familiarity
model beads using the pellet technique
decorate the beads by painting
make an ornament using beads
appreciate making beads using the pellet technique

content_topics: Text of the Kenya National Anthem
Occasions when the Kenyan National flag is hoisted (national holidays, school assemblies, heads of state visits, national meetings among others)
learning_experiences: listen to or watch a live or recorded performance of the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem in unison and sing along,
write the text of the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem and talk about the message in the stanza,
collaboratively perform the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem observing appropriate etiquette,
talk about the occasions when the Kenyan National Flag is hoisted.
key_inquiry_questions: 1 How is the Kenya National Anthem performed?
2 What can one learn from the Kenya National Anthem?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner keenly listens to, and talks about the words of the Kenya National Anthem.
Citizenship: the learner takes pride in performing the Kenya National Anthem.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: the learner performs the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem observing the anthem’s etiquette.
Unity: the learner performs the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem with peers.
Patriotism: the learner internalizes the message of the Kenya National Anthem developing love for the country.
sub_strands.pcis: Life skills: the learner applies the knowledge acquired in observing anthem etiquette in daily life.
sub_strands.links: Kiswahili Language Activities: the learner sings the first stanza of the Kenyan National Anthem articulating the words in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify the text of the first stanza of the Kenya National Anthem in Kiswahili
describe the message in the Kenya National anthem
identify occasions when the Kenya National Flag is raised
sing the Kenya National Anthem observing the anthem’s etiquette
appreciate the performance of the Kenya National Anthem for patriotism. 112 112

learning_experiences: observe pictures of different water points and water bodies within your locality and share them with peers,
talk about the dangers of water points and water bodies in your locality with peers,
talk about ways of observing safety around water points and water bodies in your locality,
key_inquiry_questions: How safe are the water points and water bodies in your locality?
Why is water safety awareness important?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner talks about the dangers of water points and water bodies in your locality with peers.
Learning to Learn: the learner learns to observe safety measures around different water points and water bodies in the locality. 114 114
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner observes safety precautions around water points and water bodies in their locality.
Integrity: the learner exercises self-discipline around water points and water bodies within their locality.
sub_strands.pcis:
Health Promotion: the learner practises self-discipline around water points and water bodies in their locality to avoid injuries.
Safety: the learner develops water safety awareness by practising safety measures around water points and water bodies in their locality.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental Activities: the learner practises water safety awareness within their locality.
Religious Activities: the learner applies values of self-discipline around water points and water bodies in their locality.

outcomes.text: identify different water points and water bodies in the locality
explain water dangers arising from water points and water bodies in the locality
narrate ways of observing safety around water points and water bodies in the locality
appreciate water safety in the locality for life skills
